gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Noto Sans Wancho brings a hulking lowercase, like chalk pressed hard, while Eater spits out thin strokes and wide gaps between letters. Over a full page, that sturdy sans would feel dense and clean.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-old-tu: Ornate and literary, with letters that never pinch shut. Almendra Display does its best work with its pronounced x-height, while Noto Sans Old Turkic keeps chunky, tall lowercase and open curves clear.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Futuristic and tech-minded, Audiowide runs one pen line throughout, with glyphs spaced like tiles with wide grout lines. Noto Sans Ol Chiki makes solid word blocks, curve tails held back.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Noto Sans Old Italic sits close to cap height with open curve endings, under Audiowide's tiled, unit-width futuristic strokes. Long paragraphs in it would feel compact, tidy and contemporary.
gen-eater-gf-parkinsans: Dark and snarling, with gaps between every letter. Eater does menace best, with a modest stem-to-hairline contrast, while Parkinsans does small, crisp sizes best with one stroke thickness throughout.
gen-eater-gf-prompt: Gnarly and wide-spaced, Eater snarls with thin and weighty strokes that feel related, while Prompt's lowercase looks oversized. Open apertures give Prompt a readable edge that holds the whole pairing together.
gen-flavors-gf-pt-sans-caption: Whimsical Flavors gives diagonals the same heft as stems and a towering x-height, while PT Sans Caption brings big lowercase. Those unclosed, inviting bowls are the pair's real draw.
gen-flavors-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big has a monoline skeleton, terminals finishing well away from the stem, and an x-height that fills the line. Flavors earns its keep big and short, whimsical and commanding.
gen-gf-gabarito-fs-asap: Asap reads smoothly, its lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals. Gabarito, drawn as if with one nib, brings expressive, distinctive character, and Asap keeps the page grounded beside it.
gen-gf-gabarito-fs-epilogue: Expressive Gabarito looks drawn with one nib, its terminals cut open so counters flow outward. And Epilogue adds curvy, unclamped letters on a wire-like monoline frame with a taller lowercase.
